newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says 1996 deliveries surge 9.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: VW says 1996 deliveries surge 9.7 pct.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday it delivered nearly four million vehicles to customers around the world in 1996 and grabbed for the first time at least 10 percent of the world passenger vehicle market.
VW said it delivered 3.966 million vehicles to customers last year, up 11 percent from 3.560 million vehicles in 1995.

The Wolfsburg-based carmaker reported strong sales growth in most regions of the world, including western Europe where deliveries to customers rose 9.7 percent to 2.357 million vehicles. But VW's domestic market, Germany, saw weak growth as deliveries rose only 2.6 percent to 969,400 vehicles.
Volkswagen said it would launch a "new product offensive" to secure its market share as the world's fourth-largest carmaker despite continuing difficult industry conditions.
VW also said its sales would be helped by the full availablity of models launched in late 1996 - such as the Golf Passat, the Audi A3 and the Skoda Octavia.
